I'd love to hear everyone's thoughts on where things stand.

transcript.text: I reviewed the county health guidance for the pantry this week, and there are some important requirements we need to add to the draft plan. Refrigerated food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or colder, and temperatures need to be logged every 2 hours while the pantry is open — not just weekly as the draft currently proposes. The guidance also requires sealed packages to display allergen labels. I have the printed guidance in my health-office binder and haven't yet added it to the draft.

transcript.text: I completed family outreach this week, and I need to share what I found before we finalize the plan. The participating households told me that Thursday from 5:00 to 7:00 p.m. is the only pickup window that works for them — not Wednesday lunch, as the draft currently proposes. Also, intake materials need to be available in English, Spanish, and Somali — the draft only covers English and Spanish. I haven't yet updated the operations sheet with these results, so I wanted to make sure everyone here has this information now.

transcript.text: Thank you both for bringing this critical information to the table. Nurse Rivera, the health requirements are significant — we'll need to update the plan to reflect the 41-degree refrigeration standard, the 2-hour temperature logging interval, and the allergen labeling requirement. And Mr. Hassan, the family feedback is equally important — if Thursday evening is the only workable pickup window for participating households, we need to shift from Wednesday lunch, and we must add Somali to our intake materials. I'd like to settle the operating plan now incorporating both sets of requirements so we can move forward with implementation. Let me formalize these decisions.
